_comment: Machine-checkable pin for the vendored easy1staking-com/fn-bafin-cardano-sc tree.
Do not hand-edit any file in this directory. If upstream must be updated,
re-vendor from the new source and regenerate this manifest with
`./verify-upstream-pin.sh --regenerate`.
SecurityTokenUpstreamPinTest (offline) enforces every hash below plus the
byte-equality of the backend's resource copy of plutus.json.
SOURCE IS A WORKING TREE, NOT A COMMIT. `commit` names the BASE commit this
tree was taken from; `source_state` is `dirty-worktree`, meaning the bytes
vendored here are that commit PLUS uncommitted local changes that exist only
on the maintainer's machine at `source_path`. Consequences, deliberately:
* the ONLINE check (verify-upstream-pin.sh with no flag) CANNOT run — there
is no fetchable SHA whose tarball would match. It refuses instead of
downloading `commit` and reporting a false divergence.
* `tree_sha256` is the stand-in identity: sha256 over the sorted
`path\0sha256\n` lines of `files`. It pins the exact bytes offline and is
reproducible by anyone holding the same tree.
Once the upstream changes are committed and pushed, re-pin to that real SHA:
set source_state to `commit`, drop source_path/base_commit, and run
`./verify-upstream-pin.sh --regenerate` so the online check comes back.
NOTE ON THE FORK: this pin moved off FluidTokens/fn-bafin-cardano-sc @ 7ae4ce3
to the easy1staking-com fork, which fixes the three defects documented in
docs/UPSTREAM-BAFIN-DEFECTS.md (wrong third-party registry-node index;
positional rather than identity/index-addressed node lookup; no registration
mode on the minting-logic withdraw redeemer).
blueprint_reproduced_note: Rebuilt with `aiken build` (aiken v1.1.23+8949565) in the source repo before vendoring, so the vendored plutus.json is built from the vendored sources. All 24 validators; `aiken check`: 238 tests, 0 failures.

excluded_from_vendoring.README.md: Upstream's README is documentation only and affects no compiled artifact. Excluded from the diff in verify-upstream-pin.sh and absent from `files` below, so re-adding it makes SecurityTokenUpstreamPinTest fail with UNEXPECTED README.md.
excluded_from_vendoring..claude/: Local editor state in the maintainer's checkout, not part of the contract. Excluded so a machine-specific settings file never becomes a pinned input.

uncommitted_changes_summary: The 2026-08-19/20 security-audit hardening, the 2026-08-20 CIP-68 support change (only_permitted_assets_minted; minting_authority gained a 10th parameter `reference_asset_name`; the (100) reference NFT is mintable ONLY by RegisterMint, pinned to one PLB output at quantity 1), and a follow-up fix to that change: the reference-NFT output check is now gated on `reference_asset_name != security_asset_name` as well as on the minted quantity. Without it, disabling CIP-68 the documented way (aliasing the two names) made the check read the SECURITY token's mint and demand exactly one of it, so a non-CIP-68 token could only be registered with a first mint of 1. `aiken check`: 238 tests, 0 failures, including a falsified regression test for that case.
